pos.personaBrief: Chapman's sides were counter-attacking: opponents 'dominated territorially for no tangible reward' ('lucky Arsenal'), and his best chances came after being 'driven back' and breaking away; 'the most opportune time for scoring is immediately after repelling an attack'.

pro.personaBrief: Progression was fast and direct: forwards told to go like 'flying columns' and 'make for goal direct', James and Wadsworth hitting accurate long passes straight to the forwards.

est.personaBrief: Roles were fixed and rehearsed on the magnetic table so 'every player was fully aware of the role'; the stopper stayed in the box and Buchan was kept 'up in attack scoring goals', yet the wingers cut inside rather than hugging the line.

lar.personaBrief: Chapman called wing-running and crossing a 'senseless policy' and preferred 'inside passing'; Bastin and Hulme stood in from the touchline and cut inside to score.

blo.personaBrief: Defenders were told to 'play deep' in a 'defence in depth'; Huddersfield 'defended first and attacked later' and Arsenal retreated and funnelled, with no evidence of pressing.

mar.personaBrief: Buchan's 1925 plan gave the centre-half a zonal 'beat', but in practice 'Policeman Roberts' blotted out the centre-forward, full-backs marked wingers and wing-halves the inside-forwards; weighted to practice, man-oriented.

pla.personaBrief: 'Never mind what the other team does - this is what you are going to do': Chapman imposed his system (James had to change to fit 'those we favoured') and rarely changed the team.

res.personaBrief: A pragmatic, results-first counter-attacking style that 'traditionalists hated' but was 'highly successful'; the 'lucky Arsenal' tag shows winning mattered more than spectacle.

sis.personaBrief: The collective plan came first: James was dropped until he accepted the link role, Neil was pulled from the third team and Roberts excelled because 'he did what he was told', though play to plan 'not so as to stifle individuality'.

jog.personaBrief: Chapman prized ball control and passing in the link role (Neil 'as slow as a funeral but has ball control', James, Stephenson the 'schemer') while demanding a disciplined fitness regime and pacy wingers.

bas.personaBrief: A mix: scouting networks and young signings who played key roles early (Hapgood at 19, Bastin at 18, a strong reserve side) alongside veteran schemers and record fees for established players.

lid.personaBrief: A disciplinarian who sold Islip for bad behaviour, dropped James, policed lifestyles and took team selection from directors, while also holding player-conferences and encouraging players to 'express their views'.
